title_ar: هل ما جاز أن يكون معجزة لنبي جاز أن يكون كرامة لولي؟
title_en: May Whatever Could Be a Miracle for a Prophet Also Be a Wonder for a Friend of God?
body_ar:
لا ولا يمكن أن يقع ذلك بحال من الأحوال لو كان كذلك لجاز أن ينزل الوحي على الأولياء الذين ليسوا بأنبياء فمعجزة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الوحي المنزل إليه فلو كان كلما جاز أن يكون معجزة لنبي يجوز أن يكون كرامة لولي لادعى كثير من الناس أنهم أنزل إليهم قرءان يتلى وهذا لا يمكن أن يقع أصلا و لا يمكن أن يتصوره مؤمن لكن البحث في المسألة هو ما تصل إليه كرامات الأولياء فكرامات الأولياء حق ومن عقيدة أهل السنة والجماعة إثباتها وهي أن الله يكرم من أطاعه فالله أكرم الأكرمين وأرحم الراحمين ولا يمكن أن يتساوى لديه أهل الإيمان وأهل الكفر وهو الذي يقول في كتابه﴿أفنجعل المسلمين كالمجرمين ما لكم كيف تحكمون﴾

فمن كان من أهل التقوى والورع و العبادة والصلاح لا يمكن أن يستوي مع الفاسق المجاهر أبدا لا يمكن أن يستويا عند الله تعالى فلذلك يكرم أولياءه بما يعينهم عليه من طاعته و يشرفهم بأنواع التشريف الذي منه العلم النافع والعمل الصالح وهذه الكرامات أعظمها الاستقامة على الدين أعظم كرامة يكرم الله بها الولي استقامته على أمر الدين بحيث يملك جوارحه عما حرم الله عليه والكرامات حق لكن اختلف في مبلغها إلى أي شيء تبلغ واتفقوا على أنها لا تبلغ نزول الوحي أو وجود ولد من غير والد أو إحياء الموتى لكنها تبلغ ما دون ذلك كالعلم من غير تعلم وكالعون على الطاعة كطي المسافات ووجود الأموال من غير تسبب ونحو ذلك فهذا حاصل فعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه طوي صوته مسافة شاسعة ما بين المدينة و بين فارس حين نادى سارية ابن زنيم فقال يا سارية الجبل الجبل وهذا الحديث أخرجه أحمد في فضائل الصحابة بعدة أسانيد أحدها إسناد صحيح وقد أخرجه ابن وهب في الجامع و عدد من المؤلفين في دواوين الحديث وهو حديث صحيح وكذلك فإن عثمان رضي الله عنه كان يرى أثر المعصية في وجه صاحبها فقد كان عنده أنس ابن مالك فدخل عليه رجل فقال: ما بال أحدكم يدخل علي وفي عينيه أثر الزنا فأقر الرجل فقال له أنس أوحي بعد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لا ولكنها فراسة المؤمن وكذلك الحال بالنسبة لعدد من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حصلت لهم كرامات عظيمة فالعلاء ابن الحضرمي رضي الله عنه خاض البحر فيبس أمامه حتى قطعه وكذلك فإن المرأة المهاجرة تدلى لها دلو من السماء حتى شربت منه حين ظمأها أهلها، وكذلك فإن من دونهم من التابعين حصل لهم أيضا شيء كثير من هذا بل قد قال شيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية رحمه الله إن الكرامات كلما انتقص الإيمان والعبادة في الناس وكلما انتقص العلم كلما ازدادت هي لأن الناس إذا كانوا أهل إيمان و ورع وتقوى لا يحتاجون إلى هذه الكرامات التي تزيد إيمانهم بالغيب وإذا نقص لديهم الإيمان بالغيب كثرت فيهم هذه الكرامات لأولياء الله أصحاب الإستقامة و الإلتزام بالحق ومع هذا فإن كثيرا من الناس تلتبس عليهم الكرامة بما ليس بكرامة.
body_en:
No. That cannot occur under any circumstance. If it were so, it would be possible for revelation to come down upon friends of God (awliyāʾ) who are not prophets — for the miracle of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is the revelation sent down to him. If everything that could be a miracle for a prophet could be a wonder (karāmah) for a friend of God, then many people would claim that a Qur'an to be recited had been sent down to them; and this cannot occur at all, and no believer can conceive of it.

But the point of inquiry in the question is how far the wonders of the friends of God extend. The wonders of the friends of God are real, and affirming them is part of the creed of the people of the sunnah and the community: namely that God honours those who obey Him. For God is the most generous of the generous and the most merciful of the merciful, and it is not possible that the people of faith and the people of unbelief should be equal in His sight — He who says in His Book: {Shall We then treat those who submit like the criminals? What is the matter with you? How do you judge?} (Sūrat al-Qalam 68:35–36).

So one who is of the people of God-consciousness, scrupulousness, worship and uprightness cannot ever be the equal of the open transgressor; they cannot be equal in the sight of God, exalted. For that reason He honours His friends with what helps them to obey Him, and ennobles them with kinds of ennoblement, among which are beneficial knowledge and righteous action. The greatest of these wonders is steadfastness upon the religion: the greatest wonder with which God honours a friend of His is his steadfastness in the matter of religion, such that he has mastery over his own limbs where God has made something forbidden to him. The wonders are real, but there is disagreement over their extent — how far they reach. They agreed that they do not reach the descent of revelation, nor the coming to be of a child without a father, nor the raising of the dead; but they do reach what is below that, such as knowledge without learning, and help towards obedience, such as the folding up of distances, and the appearing of money without any means being taken to it, and the like. This does occur.

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, God be pleased with him, had his voice folded across a vast distance between Medina and Persia, when he called out to Sariyah ibn Zunaym and said: 'Sariyah, the mountain! The mountain!' This report was brought out by Ahmad in Faḍāʾil al-Ṣaḥābah by several chains of transmission, one of them a sound chain; and Ibn Wahb brought it out in al-Jāmiʿ, and a number of authors in the collections of hadith; and it is a sound report. Likewise ʿUthman, God be pleased with him, used to see the trace of a sin on the face of the one who had committed it. Anas ibn Malik was with him, and a man came in upon him, and he said: 'What is the matter with one of you, that he comes in upon me with the trace of fornication in his eyes?' And the man confessed. So Anas said to him: 'Is there revelation after the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him?' He said: 'No — but it is the discernment of the believer.'

It is the same in the case of a number of the Companions of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him: great wonders occurred for them. Al-ʿAla ibn al-Hadrami, God be pleased with him, waded into the sea and it dried before him until he crossed it. And likewise the emigrant woman, for whom a bucket was let down from heaven so that she drank from it, when her own people left her thirsty. Likewise those below them among the Successors — much of this occurred for them too. Indeed the Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, God have mercy on him, said that the more faith and worship are diminished among people, and the more knowledge is diminished, the more the wonders increase — because when people are people of faith and scrupulousness and God-consciousness, they have no need of these wonders that increase their faith in the unseen; and when their faith in the unseen is diminished, these wonders become frequent among them, for the friends of God who are the people of steadfastness and of holding fast to the truth. And even so, many people confuse a wonder with what is no wonder at all.

flags.context: the pair the whole answer turns on
options: wonder (karāmah) for a friend of God, against miracle (muʿjizah) for a prophet
flags.note: Neither term is in the glossary and both should be added, since the distinction is the substance of the answer and will recur across the corpus. A muʿjizah is evidentiary, establishing prophethood; a karāmah is not. 'Saint' for walī has been avoided throughout because it imports a Christian institution of canonisation that has no counterpart here; 'friend of God' is the literal sense and is what the Sheikh's argument uses.

flags.arabic: واتفقوا على أنها لا تبلغ نزول الوحي أو وجود ولد من غير والد أو إحياء الموتى … لكن اختلف في مبلغها
flags.context: the scope of the agreement and of the disagreement
options: keep the agreed limits and the open disagreement clearly separate, as done here
present the whole passage as settled
present the whole passage as disputed
flags.note: IMPORTANT — DO NOT CLOSE WHAT HE LEFT OPEN. The Sheikh marks a precise boundary: there is consensus that wonders do not reach revelation, virgin birth or raising the dead; and there is unresolved disagreement about exactly how far below that they do reach. He gives examples of what he says does occur but does not claim the disagreement is settled. The English must keep the agreement and the disagreement apart, and must not let his examples read as a ruling on the disputed extent.

flags.arabic: فقد كان عنده أنس ابن مالك فدخل عليه رجل فقال
flags.context: the account of ʿUthman discerning a sin
options: render as the source has it, with the antecedents left as they stand
flags.note: The pronouns in this account are hard to follow as printed: it is not made explicit that the man who confesses is the one who entered, nor that 'he said: No — but it is the discernment of the believer' is ʿUthman answering Anas. The English keeps the Arabic's own looseness rather than resolving it by inserting names. The Sheikh gives no narrator, collection or grading for this account, unlike the preceding one, and none has been supplied.

flags.arabic: وهذا الحديث أخرجه أحمد في فضائل الصحابة بعدة أسانيد أحدها إسناد صحيح … وهو حديث صحيح
flags.context: the Sheikh's own documentation of the report about ʿUmar and Sariyah
options: reproduce the attribution and grading exactly as he gives them
add the grading of other authorities
flags.note: This is the one place in the record where the Sheikh documents a report fully — collection, multiple chains, a grading of one chain, corroborating collections, and an overall grading of ṣaḥīḥ. All of it has been reproduced exactly and nothing added. Note that the grading of this particular report is contested elsewhere in the literature; the Sheikh's grading is his own and stands as his.

Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
There is no question in the body; the question is in the title alone, and the body opens with the bare answer 'No'.
The Qur'anic quotation is given in the source without a reference; the reference has been supplied per house style. The wording matches Sūrat al-Qalam 68:35–36.
'The folding up of distances' renders ṭayy al-masāfāt, the technical idiom for traversing distance instantaneously; the same verb ṭuwiya is then used of ʿUmar's voice, and the English keeps the echo.
'The discernment of the believer' renders firāsat al-muʾmin, itself the wording of a well-known report, which the Sheikh does not cite as such here.
Ibn Taymiyyah's view is reported by the Sheikh without a source reference and none has been supplied. The source spells قرءان, الإستقامة and الإلتزام with connecting hamza; preserved in body_ar.
